quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection is ahead.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive in the right lane only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without emergency braking, which could cause a rear-end crash.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, nighttime driving is:
questions.explanation: Nighttime driving is more dangerous because visibility is poor, headlights can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest approach is to:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive at the same speed as other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than surrounding vehicles. Drive with the flow of traffic, within the speed limit.

questions.question: You must drive carefully near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: The person is a police officer.

questions.explanation: A white cane signals that a pedestrian is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic signal?
questions.explanation: A green left arrow means you can turn in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: You may go through a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is in your lane.
You are already in the intersection when it turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when it turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through carefully.

questions.question: If you stop on the side of the road at night, you should:

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on so other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Enter the exit lane well in advance. Slow down only after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: You see an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass. Then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both vehicles at once.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you with high beams on. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your high beams a few times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your high beams a few times.
questions.explanation: Flash your high beams quickly a few times to warn the driver. If they do not dim their lights, look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Nothing, because bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
They will always get a warning.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: A police officer is directing traffic at an intersection with a working traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: When an officer directs traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light. Officers take priority over traffic signals.

questions.question: Your tire suddenly blows out. What should you do?

options.text: Let the steering wheel move freely.
Hold the steering wheel and let the car slow down gradually.
Brake hard to stop right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel and let the car slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly. Do not brake hard. Slowly release the gas pedal and steer smoothly. Let your car slow down and pull to a safe spot.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Keep space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react. Do not crowd vehicles on your sides.

questions.question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles have:
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that cannot be seen in the mirrors.

questions.question: A driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing (no traffic light). Who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at an intersection, even without a traffic light or crosswalk.
